reviews.body:
## Updated interpretation: conditioning is the next validation target, not CPU matching

Reviewed the report, fixed-reference tables, representative per-config records, diagnostic DC kernel and source provenance at `c89e74c2`. This is a source/evidence review with bounded arithmetic cross-checks, not a fresh native campaign or independent verification of every archived member.

The revised report usefully preserves the original CPU references for the primary census, reports the separate conditioned-CPU comparison, retains regressions/global failures and qualifies the configuration-level p values. The fixed-reference 17/19/16 counts and A0→A1 discordant counts 4/6 support the stated negative result for peak fitting as the principal missing cause. The selective arithmetic fix remains valid independently.

**The strongest new conclusion is a shared numerical-conditioning weakness.** Bilateral pre-inverse CCF DC removal produces 0/60 large-disagreement screen positives, with very small native trajectory discrepancies in the 58 nonfailure configurations. CPU-only conditioning itself substantially changes products. It is therefore inappropriate to continue using the unconditioned CPU trajectory as scientific ground truth or to reject a conditioning change just because it moves away from that output.

**Equally important: the 0/60 headline is not a correctness certificate.** e10216-01 still exhausts all five global iterations with roughly 58.57 px last-increment RMSD on both conditioned paths, yet has product relative RMSE around 0.000229 and exit 0. This is a concrete shared-failure/strong-agreement counterexample. The report already discloses it; carry it into every high-level summary and any release decision. The 0.1 screen, the named backend profile, actual alignment convergence and motion-truth success are distinct outcomes. The backend profile's 0.001 relative-RMSE field is itself nonblocking per `docs/gate_contract.md`; do not infer whole-gate results from one image number.

**Next discriminating experiment:** hold the Hermitian repair and corrected scalar fit fixed and independently vary global-CCF DC removal and local-CCF DC removal (off/off, on/off, off/on, on/on). Both backends should implement the same specified operation, but the primary oracles should be analytic/high-precision correlation maps and injected motion. Compare peak contrast/curvature and absolute/local-contrast-normalized error, not raw ULP counts across pedestal and zero-mean maps, whose ULP scales differ. Add stage tests with prescribed DC changes, constant/positive-scale invariance where the guard and preprocessing assumptions permit it, and explicit no-signal/ambiguous cases.

The existing native experiment does not isolate global versus local conditioning, high-precision map formation versus five-sample fitting, or absolute motion accuracy. Preserve those as open rather than treating all residual disagreement as one fully established cause. Freeze this development corpus and use held-out movies/noise seeds for selecting and qualifying subsequent changes.

Prepare S1.4 in parallel using #61's prospective, matched-particle/half-set protocol; no requirement to drive CPU-relative error to zero before scientific testing. Preserve all historical results and qualify any changed correctness/compatibility contract explicitly, rather than weakening legacy thresholds after seeing outcomes.

title: S1: full peak-fit census and bilateral CCF conditioning evidence

reviews.body:
## Focused review and revised acceptance rationale

Reviewed the production hunk and `tests/cuda_peak_fit.cu` at `d888ab11`, alongside the retained #257 native evidence and the new #261 census. No new native GPU execution in this review.

The implementation promotes the five stored samples before the curvature calculation, retains the float threshold value, applies the existing float scale in double, and performs the final float store once. Integer selection and tie order are unchanged. The actual-kernel test and named float-denominator mutant support a genuine, localized arithmetic correction; the intended rounded-zero guard changes are now documented. I found no additional blocking production defect in this focused diff.

**Do not judge this patch by reproducing CPU movie outputs.** The useful contract is accurate evaluation of the specified parabola on the same stored samples, with an explicit fallback rule and error bounded at the final float conversion. A small exact-rational or higher-precision reference for selected finite float triplets, plus constructed parabolas with known vertices, would strengthen independence beyond copying the same expression into host double. Keep map-quantization error separate from fitting error: more precision cannot recover information already absent from the float CCF.

The complete #261 census changes the causal conclusion: #254-only to #254+this fit gives 17→19/60 fixed-reference screen positives and median maximum global discrepancy 0.038605→0.039105 px in the other 58 configurations. Thus the hypothesis that this is the main missing cause of the remaining global gap was not supported by that experiment. This does **not** negate the same-input arithmetic bug or establish worse scientific accuracy. Retain the fix's independent mathematical justification; do not advertise it as the S1 solution.

The existing known-motion results are useful bounded regression evidence: the high-SNR global/local/nonsquare gate cases pass, but the noisy case still has a visible characterization accuracy failure. `OVERALL PASS` must not be presented as low-SNR motion recovery or downstream qualification. The next #262 work should expand truth/conditioning coverage, not tune this patch until legacy CPU outputs match.

Performance remains unmeasured: expect the selective double calculation to be relatively small, but measure the real kernel and complete movie on target hardware rather than asserting zero/negligible cost. Preserve the legacy fixture failure and frozen-F identity control separately. No merge or combined scientific sign-off implied.

title: Fix #257: evaluate CUDA subpixel peak fit in double

reviews.body:
## Census / attribution review and guidance for the next experiment

I independently recalculated the screen classifications from the committed `raw/census/census_table.md` at `23a320a6` (the displayed values do not straddle the 0.1 threshold). The 4096² sample reproduces **27/60 → 17/60**, with **13 improvements / 3 regressions**, and the ordinary configuration-level exact McNemar calculation is **0.021270751953125**. This is a useful improvement over the earlier positive-only sample. No new native runs are claimed here.

### Report the sampling unit and endpoint explicitly

These are **30 movies, each tested at two grids**, not 60 independent movies. The pooled McNemar p-value assumes independence of the discordant paired observations; the within-movie grid dependence needs a sensitivity analysis. Importantly, this does not erase the observed benefit:

- Per-movie change in number of positive grids (off minus #254): **10 movies improve by 1, one improves by 2, two worsen by 1, and 17 have net change 0**. An exact paired sign-flip calculation on those movie-level count differences gives **p = 0.01953125**, under movie-level exchangeability. This is a sensitivity calculation, not randomized-trial or population proof.
- A different, user-facing endpoint, **at least one grid positive per movie**, is **19/30 → 15/30**, with **6 improvements / 2 regressions**; exact McNemar **p = 0.2890625**. Do not describe the configuration-level 37% relative reduction as a 37% reduction in failing movies.

For the next census pre-specify the endpoint, preserve both grids within movie in resampling/permutation, report per-family and per-grid continuous errors plus threshold counts, and retain all original positives and negatives. These selected families/movies are not a random sample of all acquisitions; keep population claims bounded.

### Preserve regressions and distinguish conditioning from truth

The correction creates positives as well as removing them, e.g. **10216-07 5×5 0.0371 → 0.9951**, **12963-08 5×5 0.0377 → 0.1885**, and **12963-09 3×3 0.0551 → 0.1063**. Also retain worsening within the already-positive group, e.g. **10216-08 5×5 0.2441 → 1.0452**. These do not refute the need to repair invalid C2R input, but they prevent calling the patch a universal image-quality improvement. Put these cases in the #257 ablation set.

The two equal-trajectory + projection controls support **global-trajectory propagation as an important upstream sensitivity for those movies**. They do not establish that subpixel scalar cancellation uniquely explains the remaining 17 configurations. Please narrow “what remains is ...” accordingly and retain the positive-only/all-configuration distinction.

### Random perturbation controls and h(y) attribution

The two seeds are useful **RMS-matched perturbation controls**, not a sampled null distribution that quantifies all near-tie reshuffling. Independent random row signs do not preserve the spectrum/autocorrelation of the measured h(y), which matters after filtering/cropping. A stronger optional control preserves the row term's power spectrum (for example cyclic shifts or conjugate-symmetric random phases), uses a predeclared seed set and reports per-movie changes. Keep this as diagnostic evidence, not a prerequisite to accepting the deterministic C2R invariant repair.

Describe the tested intervention precisely as **Hermitian projection of two boundary columns at the stated consumption sites**, rather than exact removal of only a row function. #250 already records non-row full-band residuals. The agreement of the two-site toggle and all-five-site #254 outcomes is bounded to these 60 configurations and tested routes; it does not prove CCF projections are universally irrelevant.

Finally, the updated #243 shared-global-failure label for 10216-01 should retain its raw CPU/CUDA metric. A shared failure mode does not make a measured inter-backend difference disappear. Show any exclusion as a secondary, explicitly scoped sensitivity analysis rather than improving the primary denominator post hoc.

Suggested follow-up: baseline / Hermitian-only / peak-only / both, from one pinned base; global-only/local-only peak ablations on the mechanism cases; then the full original census and unaffected-family controls. Keep numerical, convergence, known-truth and downstream scientific outcomes distinct.

title: docs(s1.3c): attribute S1 to the cuFFT C2R row term h(y): census with null (evidence only)

reviews.body:
## Follow-up source/test review for the active implementation agent

Reviewed the projection helper and the five production callsite changes at `8b55d5da`, plus `tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp`. I found no additional concrete production-kernel defect: pair ownership is disjoint, odd widths do not acquire a fictitious x-Nyquist column, self-paired rows are handled, and projection happens on consumption scratch rather than repeatedly altering the resident spectra. I support keeping this a narrow contract repair, separate from #257 and from a new Nyquist-resampling convention. This is source inspection, not a fresh GPU run.

The existing deterministic-invariant request is correct. **One additional test-oracle detail:** the positive reference in `tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp` currently phases the half-spectrum and passes it directly to `fftwf_plan_dft_c2r_2d` / `fftwf_execute`, without explicitly restoring Hermitian boundary conditions. Thus the positive reference also relies on the observed behavior of an out-of-contract input, not just the no-projection mutant. FFTW's documentation describes C2R on Hermitian input; generic sanitisation is not the API contract.

Please make the revised tests distinguish three claims:

1. **Portable input invariant and callsite coverage.** In a test-only instrumented build, inspect the actual buffer immediately before each of the five production C2R calls. Assert conjugacy on x=0 and x=Nx/2 when present, real self-paired bins, and finite values for the finite fixture. Use fixtures with a demonstrated nonzero pre-projection defect. Remove each callsite projection separately and require an invariant failure *before* calling the FFT. Exercise both CCF consumers and relevant global/local/retry routes; two implementations agreeing is not coverage if they share the same omission.
2. **Defined output oracle.** Independently construct/project the host reference buffer first, then use a valid real inverse or an explicit full-complex high-precision reference. Include isolated boundary modes and legitimate complex conjugate pairs, unchanged interior bins, zero/integer/fractional shifts, odd/even dimensions, idempotence and resident-buffer immutability. Keep original-byte copies because C2R may overwrite its input. Do not generate the only oracle by reusing the production projection helper.
3. **Historical A100 characterization.** Retain the observed 4096² raw-input leak and its disappearance after repair, including device/toolkit/plan details. Do not require another supported GPU/cuFFT plan to produce that same invalid-input artifact for the suite to pass.

### Why CUDA changes while CPU is currently left alone

Both paths can create incompatible boundary values. The tested FFTW implementation effectively discards that component; the measured cuFFT path can turn it into a real-image artifact. This patch makes the CUDA input valid and selects a result close to that observed CPU behavior. That is a reason to fix CUDA now, not evidence that CPU input construction is mathematically exempt. An explicit CPU-consumption projection can be considered separately with CPU regression and cost tests. Likewise, the shared fractional-Nyquist/crop-folding policy remains a separately specified scientific choice.

Use valid-input mathematical/property tests as the acceptance basis. Exact CPU equality and lower end-to-end RMSE are useful diagnostics, not the definition of correctness. After the test update, retain the exact tested SHA and affected native suites; no merge or maintainer sign-off is implied by this comment.

Primary contracts: [cuFFT 12.8 §2.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types), [FFTW multidimensional real transforms](https://www.fftw.org/fftw3_doc/Multi_002ddimensional-Transforms.html).

## Updated review: input-contract coverage improved; finish the independent output oracle

Reviewed the delta `8b55d5da..af2a5900`, `tests/cuda_hermitian_check.h`, the revised registrations and `tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp`. This is source/retained-evidence review, not a new native run.

**Resolved:** the five site-specific projection-removal mutants now test the actual consumption buffer before C2R, including both CCF consumers. The checker fails on a dedicated invariant violation, not on a particular cuFFT response to malformed input. The production projection source is unchanged. The 4096² leak is correctly retained as characterization, and the 117/118 nvCOMP run plus 1/1 fixture rerun is not relabelled as a clean full-suite pass.

**Still outstanding from the previous review:** the positive numerical reference still phases `f`, copies it directly to `fftw_input`, then executes `fftwf_plan_dft_c2r_2d` without restoring boundary conjugacy (`tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp`, approximately lines 76–88 at this head). Thus the negative test is now portable, but the output oracle still relies on FFTW's observed handling of invalid input. The separate injection program's projected-input controls do not change this production-path test reference.

Please independently project the host reference before its real inverse, or use an explicitly defined full-complex high-precision inverse of a valid spectrum. Keep the unprojected FFTW result as an optional compatibility observation only. For small isolated modes, an analytic/direct-DFT oracle is stronger than a second implementation of the same helper.

Also make the positive tests discriminate **the selected projection**, not only symmetry: valid complex-conjugate boundary signal and interior bins must be preserved, self-paired bins must be real, and a mutant that zeros entire boundary columns must fail. A buffer of zeros is Hermitian too; invariant checks alone do not establish the correct operator. Retain odd/even geometry, multiple frames, idempotence, scratch-only behavior and resident-byte preservation.

**Updated acceptance principle:** accept this narrow repair because every inverse receives the specified mathematically valid representation and matches an independent valid-input oracle. Exact agreement with current CPU output is not the goal. The shared CPU input-contract issue is now #266; the fractional-Nyquist/crop-folding convention remains separately specified and tested rather than silently altered here. Do not require subpixel phase composition/energy preservation at Nyquist unless the chosen interpolation convention actually guarantees it; those are clean tests for strictly sub-Nyquist inputs.

The new injection evidence is consistent with constant and alternating-x leakage on the tested 4096² implementation. It strengthens the mechanism characterization, but inspecting cuFFT internals or proving a scientific interpolation policy is not necessary to justify fixing the input contract.

Primary contracts: [cuFFT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types), [FFTW](https://www.fftw.org/fftw3_doc/Multi_002ddimensional-Transforms.html). No merge, tolerance change or scientific sign-off implied.

reviews.body:
Reviewed production accounting, error/resource handling, the small regression control and retained native evidence at 4c82012b. I found no blocking defect. The full-spectrum/CCF/shift counts and queried C2R plan match the actual nonresident global-aligner allocations and geometry. The plan is released before free memory is rechecked, and the documented necessary-memory check does not promise protection against fragmentation or concurrent allocations.

I checked the raw 74/109/112 full-suite receipts, all eight named early-refusal records, the passing strict-product comparison reports, and current-head CI (both jobs pass; CUDA CI is compile-only). The 4cd85167-to-head comparison contains no src/ or CMake changes, so the native-tested implementation remains applicable. The preserved first CPU environment failure is correctly distinguished from its complete passing rerun.

Nonblocking test hardening: CudaEarlyStreamingOom's one-byte budget deliberately skips the new cuFFT planning branch. The retained 21 GiB probes cover successful planning followed by refusal, but focused wrappers for CUFFT_ALLOC_FAILED, other plan errors and fatal runtime state during plan creation/destruction would protect the new classifier/cleanup boundary. In particular, assert that an earlier fatal planning status cannot be obscured by cleanup and then reported as ordinary OOM. This is a coverage recommendation; I did not reproduce a misclassification.

title: #226 D3: refuse insufficient CUDA memory before host preprocessing

reviews.body:
The new native captures expose an avoidable arithmetic effect in the peak path itself. This is stronger evidence than the toy example in #232, so I would qualify “no CUDA defect found” / “all rounding” before treating S1.3 as causal closure.

Concrete same-input witness at this head: raw/runs/e10216-p3-diag-{cpu,cuda}-on/ccf.txt.gz, global iteration 1, frame 56. Both backends select (0,0); all five captured float32 map samples are bit-identical. For x, m=36366.4296875, vp=36365.69140625, vn=36366.359375, with scale=4. The existing CUDA expression rounds vp+vn before subtracting 2*m, producing denominator -0.8125; evaluating the identical stored samples in double gives -0.80859375. Native CUDA x=-1.6442307233810425; native CPU x=-1.6521739130434783. This 0.00794319 px difference needs neither different FFT samples nor an integer peak/tie change.

I replayed all 32,195 CUDA records, including retries, converting the nine-significant-digit samples back to float32 and using the logged patch sizes/CCF dimensions, holding the GPU's float32 scale fixed across variants:
- Explicit float32 evaluation of the existing expression reproduces every recorded native x/y candidate exactly.
- Replacing only the denominator with (vp-m)+(vn-m), retaining float32 throughout and the same winner/guard/scale, gives the exact double denominator on all 64,390 recorded axes.
- Largest absolute candidate-component difference from the double evaluation of the same samples falls from 0.13525164 px to 0.000002646 px. The larger example is 10474F3 patch (1,5), iteration 4, frame 6; its retry repeats it.
- Already in global iteration 1, the largest same-input component effect is 0.0170694 px (10641b, reference frame 1). For 10216 it is the 0.00794319 px witness above.
- No guard branch changes, non-finite values, or zero-denominator repairs occurred in this captured set. One search-boundary record has a neighbor above the selected maximum; it was included, not discarded.

These are host scalar replays of native captured samples, not a native run of a proposed fix. They isolate avoidable evaluation-order loss on an already-quantized CCF; they do not measure the unknown unquantized peak, prove the entire S1 mismatch is fixed, or remove the observed near-tie mechanism. In the key 10216 (2,1), iteration 2, frame 1 event, the corresponding same-input y correction is only 0.00844582 px, much smaller than that event's different-integer-peak jump.

A useful next paired experiment is current expression vs stable float32 differences vs promoting just the five samples/fit to double, from identical captured maps first and then through the complete iterative run with unchanged tie rules, convergence threshold and image gates. Please include exactly flat/one-ULP plateaus, ties, search-boundary neighbors, near-guard/subnormal inputs and compiler reassociation in a regression check before choosing an implementation. The finite captured set is not a proof of universal guard equivalence. This should let us distinguish ordinary backend map differences from this separately demonstrated, avoidable arithmetic contribution.

A separate attribution/scope point from the analysis scripts: the evidence supports the near-tie mechanism, but the current “patch-input differences are the global trajectory difference, propagated” and “phase shift is not the cause” wording is stronger than the measured controls.

1. phasefit.py reports hypot(fitted_translation + global_trajectory_delta). That is agreement between two translation estimates, not the residual phase left after fitting. It does not measure the component of phase error orthogonal to the two translation columns. The committed direct ramp test makes this important: summary.json reports 12963 input relative difference 0.00635078 before versus 0.00620990 after correction, and 10474F3 0.00590086 versus 0.00580159. Those aggregate medians retain about 97.8% and 98.3% of the original difference. This does not disprove the proposed crop explanation, but it does leave it untested. Please label the quoted “residual px” as translation-estimate disagreement and also report a weighted phase-fit residual.

2. analyze.py shift_test only evaluates a transition when the next iteration's input exists. Consequently the final shift of a converged global iteration is outside this test, as are frequencies outside the CCF window. That final full spectrum is what the subsequent global inverse FFT and patch crop consume (runner around 3404–3488 and 3792–3802). Spatial cropping mixes frequencies, so the reported <=5.7e-7 inter-iteration window error is not a bound on the full upstream operation that supplies patch inputs.

The discriminating control is a 2x2 replay from one shared full-frame spectrum: CPU/CUDA shift-and-reconstruction operators crossed with the two prescribed global trajectories, followed by identical crop/group/FFT. Holding trajectory fixed separates backend arithmetic; swapping trajectory on one backend measures propagation including crop amplitude changes. This would turn the currently inferred link into a measured one.

Two targeted follow-ons now have unusually strong motivation:
- For the demonstrated curvature effect, a native same-map test followed by GPU baseline/global-only/local-only/both stable-curvature diagnostic arms would distinguish upstream seeding from late local contribution. Keep the existing selection, convergence and output gates.
- For DC conditioning, both CPU and CUDA retain the DC term in the leave-one-out CCF. Zero only the CCF spectrum's (0,0) term before inverse FFT as a diagnostic control. In exact arithmetic this only subtracts a spatial constant and preserves peak locations/quadratic curvature. In float32, the retained pedestal can lose contrast before the selector sees it; the README's “uniform offset cannot change ... quadratic step” needs that exact-arithmetic qualification. Subtracting the mean after the float32 inverse cannot recover contrast already lost.

The scalar result in my earlier review was also independently checked with a separate struct.pack/unpack float32 implementation directly on the raw records: every native candidate reproduced, and the same denominator/guard results held. None of these replays is a native run of the proposed changes.

Fit-level cross-check: I reproduced the published counterfactuals from the ten production STARs and added a common-accepted-patch control. On the same 33x33 grid/all-frame definition, restricting both refits to the intersection of accepted patches changes max/rms field differences as follows:
- 10216 5x5: 7.401/1.628 -> 0.221/0.033 px.
- 10474F3: 7.445/1.578 -> 0.053/0.015 px.
- 10641: 94.323/18.403 -> 0.400/0.075 px.
- 12963: 9.477/1.479 -> 3.187/0.668 px; substantial differences in common accepted trajectories remain.
- 10216 3x3 is unchanged, as expected because all nine patches are common.

This supports acceptance-set/model extrapolation sensitivity as a major downstream amplifier in three 5x5 cases. It is not evidence that the 94 px field difference is a least-squares arithmetic error. Every fitted design has rank 18; column-normalized condition numbers are about 202–365, and column-scaled versus unscaled float64 refits differ by <3e-10 px on this grid. These remain host fit-only controls; corrected images have not been regenerated.

There is also a specific explanation for the up-to-0.38 px refit_reproduces_star discrepancy. metadata_table.cpp:257–276 formats negative doubles with only five digits after the decimal (scientific only below magnitude 0.001 or above 100000). In the 10641 CPU STAR, coefficient index 8, x²z³, is stored as -0.00122; the refit gives -0.00122271287007. Applying the writer's exact formatting to the refit reduces its field discrepancy against the stored STAR from 0.356601 to 0.000122 px on CPU and from 0.382139 to 0.000200 px on CUDA. Cubic time dependence makes this serialization loss visible.

Please distinguish the quantities explicitly: fitattr.py:86–89 computes cpu_vs_cuda and swaps from fresh refits of rounded STAR observations; only refit_reproduces_star compares those fits with serialized coefficients. For an exact native-model check, capture full-precision in-memory coefficients before STAR formatting. The serialization loss is a separate round-trip concern, not an explanation for the already-written native MRC mismatch. Reporting common-patch refits and full-image versus observed-patch-region fields would make the acceptance/extrapolation mechanism especially clear.

Reviewed the S1.3b delta at 7fc9733f. The 16 retained runs all exit 0, all eight CUDA runs witness the intended UUID, and all 12 retained identity comparisons pass. The equal-trajectory/full-spectrum controls materially improve the diagnosis. Two details matter before implementing a remedy.

1. This is an input-contract problem, not a demonstrated cuFFT library defect. The CUDA 12.8 documentation explicitly requires Hermitian input for multidimensional C2R and says behavior is undefined otherwise: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types . Fractionally phase-shifting the stored boundary columns without restoring their conjugacy can violate that precondition in exact arithmetic. The native row term is therefore evidence of a real application-level numerical/representation issue; it should not be classified as ordinary float32 roundoff or as a portable property of cuFFT. “Present whenever x-shift is fractional” also needs qualification: its size depends on the Nyquist content and can vanish.

2. The full-frame residual is not entirely a row constant. In raw/s13b/analysis/*-fullframe.json, frame 11 has after_removing_row_means_rms:
- 10216: 0.0036416573, or 1.0696e-4 relative to frame RMS.
- 12963: 0.0003972494, or 3.0129e-4 relative.
Subtracting the row mean is the least-squares best possible row-only correction, so these are lower bounds for subtracting any h(y) from that CPU/CUDA real-frame difference. Both records also show a non-Hermitian kx=0 column. The <=5.8e-7 hpredict residual concerns cropped low-frequency CCF-window spectra and cannot certify the full image. Please retain separate low-window and full-band residual claims, and identify the source/metric for the README's 2e-6/6e-8 full-frame residual statement.

A targeted next native test would feed identical saved spectrum bytes to both inverse paths, then repeat after projecting BOTH self-conjugate boundary columns: kx=0, plus kx=nx/2 when nx is even. For each such column use H[ky]=(F[ky]+conj(F[-ky mod ny]))/2; self-paired ky=0 and, when even, ny/2 become real. Preserve the legitimate Hermitian component rather than zeroing the whole Nyquist column. First compare to the explicitly defined real-valued reference, then rerun the equal-trajectory patch/acceptance/product controls. Include integer/fractional x-only, y-only and combined shifts, even/odd dimensions, and isolated boundary modes.

The additional full-band residual may be an alternating-x component associated with the kx=0 violation; packed real-FFT algorithms can mix invalid DC/Nyquist imaginary components. That is a hypothesis to test with an isolated-mode witness, not a claim about cuFFT internals. Repairing only the observed h(y) after inverse could leave the C2R contract violation and other components intact.

The earlier same-input peak-curvature finding remains a separate demonstrated arithmetic contribution. These new controls do not yet quantify how much either mechanism contributes to the final scientific outcome.

One implementation-scope addition to the Hermitian check: please also instrument the actual reduced-grid CCF spectrum before its C2R, not just the full-frame global spectrum.

computeReferenceKernel/computeCCFKernel copy the original frequency window into the smaller ccf_nx/ccf_ny geometry (cuda_alignpatch.cu:140–179; corresponding CPU runner:4747–4772). A valid full-image Hermitian spectrum need not be valid at the new crop boundaries. For example, when cropping a 16-row spectrum to 8 rows, original ky=+4 becomes the new self-conjugate Nyquist row; its original conjugate at ky=-4 is not folded into that cell. At kx=0 the copied coefficient can therefore remain complex. The new last x column has the analogous conjugate-pair requirement. The kernels do not enforce those conditions before inverse.

This is a source-level contract risk, not a measured extra cause of S1: the B weights suppress boundary content, and the retained <=9.4-ulp own-input map comparisons remain valid observations. But fixing only the full-frame global inverse would not prove all C2R inputs are valid. Record conjugacy residuals at both actual CCF boundary columns and compare a boundary-projected same-buffer control, preserving all interior bins and existing gates. That will distinguish the measured global reconstruction problem from any smaller crop-boundary contribution without changing weights or guessing from total-map norms.

title: docs(s1.3): CCF near-tie logging, CPU vs CUDA local alignment (evidence only)

reviews.body:
Source and retained-evidence review at 84872649: no new correctness blocker found in the production change. Full-read detection selects every header-declared frame, finish() drains and checks decoder status before alignment/publication, and clearing pipe ownership before throwing avoids a second close. The explicit subset boundary preserves early-close behavior. Retained controls cover late decoder failure separately from short reads, with strict healthy-product comparisons; I did not rerun the binaries.

Both current-head CI jobs have now passed (run 39264582920; CUDA is compile-only). The recorded native CUDA suite correctly remains 110/111 with the separately attributed #246 timeout pair; the historical result should stay unchanged after the harness fix lands.

Integration is now the remaining blocker: #247 merged into main as 36913740, and GitHub reports this PR as conflicting. Both branches append their post-RC0 entry at the same end of docs/release/RC0_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md. Reconcile by retaining both the new #246 entry and this #214 evidence/limits, then recheck the resulting head and CI. Do not resolve the documentation conflict by replacing main's post-RC0 section wholesale.

title: Fix #214: reject late compressed MRC decoder failures

reviews.body:
Source and retained-evidence review at bbca3838; no new native run performed. I found no blocking correctness issue in the identity guard. Pinning the tag-scan descriptor avoids a separate stat/open race, and checking both the pathname and reader descriptors catches replacement while an old inode remains open. The new post-upload early returns also reach ScratchScope/endIngestScratch, which drains both streams before the host fallback can reuse the Fourier arena or pinned staging.

One useful nonblocking control to add: mutate on a later chunk, after an earlier chunk has actually been converted into d_Iframes/d_Isum. The current tag-close, reader-open and first strip-read mutations all precede the first decode; a regression that checks identity only on the first chunk could therefore still pass all six rows. With the existing two-frame chunk setting, a delayed mutation plus a witness of earlier conversion would test that partial nvCOMP accumulation is discarded and the complete compact result matches the host reference.

The retained fixed/reversed controls discriminate the identity guard rather than merely accepting any fallback, and the G/L tutorial comparisons support the bounded healthy-path invariance claim. The documented immutable-input precondition and lack of arbitrary corrupt-Deflate protection remain important.

title: Fix #215: pin TIFF identity across nvCOMP ingest

reviews.body:
Source/evidence review at 6530c96d: no blocking finding in the ownership change. Value-owned addresses make exception copies independent and let unprinted exceptions release their storage; printing no longer consumes the exception. The regression uses runtime checks rather than assert, so the copy/assignment/repeated-print checks remain active in Release. The before/after sanitizer records cover the leak separately from the old use-after-free.

One small regression-hardening follow-up: add RelionErrorOwnership and RelionErrorUnprinted to DEFAULT_REQUIRED_TESTS in tools/validate_test_collection.py. They are currently additive, so accidentally losing their CMake registrations can still pass the collection gate. Also keep the sanitizer lane distinct: the ordinary uninstrumented --unprinted test cannot itself detect a leak.

Both current-head CI jobs now pass. The retained CPU 75/76 remains accurately recorded; #247's separate compiler-presence control supports the stated attribution without changing that historical result. This review did not rerun native tests.

title: Fix #239: own RelionError backtraces across exception copies

reviews.body:
Reviewed source and retained evidence at 88444f3e. The real 700/700 witness and compiled refusal mutant support the bounded containment result, and both current-head CI jobs pass (CUDA CI is compile-only). I found one cancellation-safety issue in the new test driver, detailed inline. This does not invalidate the recorded successful native runs or establish a production containment defect.

Nonblocking test strengthening: fault_verdict currently looks for each later movie name anywhere in the combined console/logs. The startup listing already contains both names, so a final failure record that omits or duplicates an attribution could still pass. Parsing the final failure record and checking the exact expected movie set, with a deliberately corrupted-attribution predicate control, would make the three-movie claim independently discriminating.

title: test(cuda): add isolated genuine sticky-context control (#213)

reviews.body:
Reviewed `d31a60dc`: the 32 frozen comparison/analysis pairs agree on the reported metrics and gate statuses; the six older CPU exact controls report complete-coverage PASS; all 76 retained run records have exit 0 and all 38 CUDA records have the requested UUID. Paired input/gain/STAR hashes agree. This is an audit of committed evidence and source, not a native rerun.

The most useful new S1.3 target is **10216, 3×3**: all nine patches are accepted on both backends, yet relative RMSE is 0.196182 (absolute RMSE 4.08598; maximum pixel error 66.7738), while the global-shift gate passes. The [comparator record](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/d31a60dc43c920d7c29a6b5e7fb2777431dbdd11/docs/post_rc0/s1/sweep/evidence/analysis/e10216-00-p3-F-cuda-backend.json) therefore provides a clean way to investigate trajectory/fit differences without a changed accepted-patch set. It does not yet distinguish bad trajectory observations from fit conditioning or downstream interpolation.

For the “real numerical issue versus expected float32 differences” question, there are two separate established facts:
- Native runs show large end-to-end differences and the earlier #212 ablations show amplification by the shared estimator. Neither fact identifies the first arithmetic discrepancy or a scientifically better backend.
- #232 already isolates **avoidable expression-level loss on identical float32 input samples**: a unique-peak triplet gives 1/8 pixel with the CUDA-style float curvature expression and 1/6 with promoted evaluation. That witness is host evidence, not evidence that this mechanism causes the 0.196–0.808 native results. I checked current main `c8844894`: `cuda_alignpatch.cu` and `cuda_realspace_dw.cu` have the same blob hashes as the #232 audit revision, so those arithmetic/coordinate mechanisms have not disappeared in RC0.

A discriminating S1.3 handoff would:
1. Capture matched patch/frame/iteration state **before feedback diverges**, including the spectra and weights entering CCF formation. Comparing later maps after different shifts have already been applied cannot isolate FFT roundoff.
2. Cross-feed each captured, identical float32 CCF to the CPU and native CUDA selector/subpixel routines. Record the actual winner, the best distinct local maximum, and the axis-neighbor triplets/curvature. This separates #70 tie semantics and scalar fit arithmetic from map-generation differences; a top-two-pixels log alone can merely describe adjacent samples of one broad peak.
3. Reuse common spectra/weights for the inverse-FFT comparison, then common frame/model inputs for interpolation. Keep those stage results separate from a full pipeline rerun and from known-motion/scientific accuracy.
4. Include a **diagnostic DC-conditioning control**. The earlier 10216 watch record has CCF values near 36,378 and a competing-peak margin of zero on CPU versus about five float32 ulps on CUDA. Measure DC/baseline and local contrast, and compare removing DC before inverse transformation with a higher-precision reference. In exact arithmetic a common offset cannot reorder peaks or change quadratic curvature; in float32 it consumes representable resolution. Subtracting an offset after the map has been quantized cannot restore lost information. This is a hypothesis to test, not an attribution or a proposed production/default change.

The breadth/longevity claims are appropriately bounded at this head. I would preserve the current gates and keep S1’s cause open until those common-input controls separate ordinary backend rounding, avoidable precision loss, and estimator amplification. Downstream S1.4 remains necessary to assess scientific consequence.
